what: Derive Place-Based Exposures from a Gaia Database in R
title: Derive Place-Based Exposures from a Gaia Database in R
text: gaiaCore R package working Gaia database. connects gaiaDB (PostgreSQL PostGIS) directly DatabaseConnector, runs Gaia pipeline R, provides analytics turn result evidence: linking place-based exposures (air pollution, deprivation, green space, anything geometry period) people OMOP CDM. gaiaCore can ingest datasets registered Gaia catalog build geometry attribute tables, load person locations residence histories (data frames OMOP CDM Gaia extension), derive exposure joining locations geospatial sources space time (EXTERNAL_EXPOSURE rows), one variable time, check derived rows (duplicates, values outside residence interval, missing implausible values, unit mismatches), copy result CDM, HADES tools CohortMethod FeatureExtraction can use , analyse exposure: day-weighted exposure windows pregnancy, effect estimates whose confidence intervals stay valid , unbalanced geographic clusters. spatial processing happens inside gaiaDB; gaiaCore calls SQL functions, every derived value stays traceable catalog entry, geometry residence interval produced .

Docker. image ohdsi/gaia-core HADES (RStudio, CohortMethod, FeatureExtraction, Capr) gaiaCore, CaprForExtensions, FeatureExtractionForExtensions, JDBC driver spatial packages (sf others) installed: Open http://localhost:8787 sign ohdsi. gaiadocker_default network database reachable gaia-db, package default; pass database password createGaiaConnectionDetails(password = ) set GAIA_POSTGRES_PASSWORD ~/.Renviron.

title: Derive Place-Based Exposures from a Gaia Database in R
text: exposure row records came : exposure_source_value variable_source_id variable (see listVariables()), exposure_relationship_source_value spatial operator, exposure_type_concept_id kind data source passed spatialJoin().
code: library(gaiaCore)  connection <- connectGaia(createGaiaConnectionDetails(server = "gaia-db/gaiacore"))  # 1. Ingest the datasets (boundaries first) and build their geometry and attribute tables ingestDatasource(connection, "us_2023_county_tl") ingestDatasource(connection, "us_2014_2019_monthly_pm25_by_county_cdc") loadVariables(connection, "us_2014_2019_monthly_pm25_by_county_cdc", geomLabel = "name", variableNodata = -999)  # 2. Load the persons' locations and residence history, and validate them loadLocationsFromOmop(connection, cdmSchema = "omopgis") validateLocations(connection)  # 3. Join locations to one variable in space and time spatialJoin(connection, "pm25_mean_pred", "us_2014_2019_monthly_pm25_by_county_cdc",             exposureTypeConceptId = 2052499878)   # Exposure Type Concept: Air Quality Database  # 4. Check the result and copy it into the CDM summarizeExposure(connection) checkExposure(connection, valueRange = c(0, 200)) copyExposureToOmop(connection, cdmSchema = "omopgis")  disconnectGaia(connection)

title: Derive Place-Based Exposures from a Gaia Database in R
text: fitExposureEffect() reports log-odds per unit exposure leave-one-cluster-jackknife interval default. simulations tract-level benchmark 175 unbalanced county clusters 95% intervals covered true value 95.8% time, 90% usual clustered sandwich interval 74% model-based intervals; interval = "glmm" fits mixed model instead.
code: # Mean exposure during a pregnancy: partial months at both ends count for the days they cover exposure <- getExposure(connection, conceptId = 2052499839) dayWeightedExposure(exposure, windows)   # windows: person_id, window_start, window_end  # Effect of exposure on an outcome, with a confidence interval that accounts for clustering by county fitExposureEffect(outcome ~ pm25 + ses + age + female, data, exposure = "pm25", cluster = "county")

title: Effect of an exposure on a binary outcome, with intervals that hold up with few clusters — fitExposureEffect
text: formula model formula 0/1 outcome, example y ~ pm25 + ses + age + female. data data frame. exposure Name exposure term whose coefficient reported. cluster Name column data identifies clusters, vector cluster ids. interval "jackknife" (default): leave-one-cluster-standard error, t quantile. "cr1": clustered sandwich standard error, t quantile. "model": model-based standard error, normal quantile (ignores clustering). "glmm": logistic mixed model random intercept cluster (lme4::glmer(), needs lme4 package), Wald interval. level Confidence level.

title: Effect of an exposure on a binary outcome, with intervals that hold up with few clusters — fitExposureEffect
text: one-row data frame estimate, se, lower, upper, level, method, n_clusters n. Coefficients log-odds per unit exposure.

title: Effect of an exposure on a binary outcome, with intervals that hold up with few clusters — fitExposureEffect
code: set.seed(1) d <- data.frame(county = rep(1:30, each = 40), x = rnorm(1200)) d$y <- rbinom(1200, 1, plogis(-1 + 0.3 * d$x + rep(rnorm(30, sd = 0.3), each = 40))) fitExposureEffect(y ~ x, d, exposure = "x", cluster = "county") #>    estimate         se     lower     upper level    method n_clusters    n #> 1 0.2325906 0.05609663 0.1178601 0.3473211  0.95 jackknife         30 1200
